Open-source tools on my shortlist

The open-source projects I'd look at first for common small-business needs, what each is for, and what to check before relying on one.

Type
Comparison
Edition
1.0
First written
November 1, 2026
Updated
November 9, 2026
Facts checked
November 1, 2026
Download PDF View source

A shortlist, not a recommendation

These are projects I'd look at first when a need is real. I reviewed their repositories, purpose, and licenses in November 2026. That's discovery, not a production test, a security review, or a promise that any of them suits your business. "Free" software still costs someone's time to host, update, and back up. The technology decisions standard explains how a tool earns its place.

How to read this

  • Worth a small trial means a sensible first look when the need exists, often with a hosted version you can pay for instead of running it yourself.
  • Needs an owner means it can be excellent but asks for real technical or domain ownership to run well.
  • In use here means neon1's own public repositories use it today.

Projects that usually cost more to run than they save at small-business scale were left off. So were any with an unresolved concern at review time.

Automation

ProjectWhat it's forFit
n8nVisual workflows that connect business toolsWorth a small trial. Source-available license, so read its terms before hosting it for others
ActivepiecesVisual automation, similar in spirit to ZapierWorth a small trial
Kestra, Windmill, Node-REDOrchestration and event-driven flowsNeeds an owner

Business applications

ProjectWhat it's forFit
TwentyA modern customer relationship managerWorth a small trial
Invoice NinjaQuotes, invoices, and paymentsWorth a small trial
Akaunting, DolibarrAccounting and small business managementNeeds an owner, and your accountant's agreement

Internal tools and databases

ProjectWhat it's forFit
NocoDB, BaserowSpreadsheet-style databases with forms and viewsWorth a small trial
Appsmith, ToolJet, BudibaseSimple internal apps on top of existing dataWorth a small trial

Documents and collaboration

ProjectWhat it's forFit
Paperless-ngxScanning, reading, and filing paper documentsWorth a small trial
Outline, BookStack, DocmostA team wiki for procedures and how-tosWorth a small trial
FormbricksSurveys and feedback formsWorth a small trial
DocumensoElectronic signaturesNeeds an owner. Check that its signatures meet your legal needs

Data and reporting

ProjectWhat it's forFit
Metabase, EvidenceDashboards and reports from your dataWorth a small trial
DuckDB, dltFast local analysis, and loading data between systemsWorth a small trial
Supabase, Airbyte, pgvectorApp backends, data pipelines, and vector searchNeeds an owner

Monitoring

ProjectWhat it's forFit
Uptime KumaSimple uptime checks and alertsWorth a small trial. Don't host it on the server it watches
SentryError tracking for appsWorth a small trial, often as the hosted service
Grafana, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry CollectorMetrics, dashboards, and tracingNeeds an owner

Backup

ProjectWhat it's forFit
restic, KopiaEncrypted backups with versionsWorth a small trial, with a test restore
rcloneCopying files to and between cloud storageWorth a small trial

Security checks

ProjectWhat it's forFit
gitleaksFinding secrets committed to codeIn use here
Trivy, Grype, SyftFinding known vulnerabilities, and listing software componentsWorth a small trial
Semgrep, CheckovCode and infrastructure scanningWorth a small trial
ZAP, ProwlerWeb app testing and cloud account reviewNeeds an owner, and agreed scope before any scan

Infrastructure and testing

ProjectWhat it's forFit
TerraformCloud infrastructure as codeIn use here
OpenTofuAn open-source fork of TerraformWorth a small trial
PlaywrightBrowser testing, and printing these PDFsIn use here
Lighthouse, axe-corePerformance and accessibility checksWorth a small trial
TailscalePrivate network access without opening portsWorth a small trial, usually as the hosted service

AI

ProjectWhat it's forFit
OllamaRunning AI models on your own machineWorth a small trial. Local doesn't automatically mean private
LangflowBuilding AI workflows visuallyWorth a small trial
promptfoo, DeepEval, Ragas, Langfuse, PhoenixTesting and monitoring AI systemsWorth a small trial, checked against a human-graded set
Dify, Open WebUI, LlamaIndex, HaystackAI apps and document searchNeeds an owner. Some carry branding or multi-tenant conditions in their licenses

Design and planning

ProjectWhat it's forFit
Excalidraw, MermaidSketches and diagramsWorth a small trial
PenpotInterface designWorth a small trial
Kanboard, VikunjaSimple task boardsWorth a small trial

Before you rely on any of these

  1. Read the license at the version you'd use, and check the terms of any hosted version separately.
  2. Confirm it's maintained and how security problems are reported.
  3. Try one real task with made-up data, then a failure, an export, and a restore.
  4. Count the hours to run it, not only the price.
  5. Write down who owns it and how you'd leave.

The tool decision form is the record I keep for each one.

Sources

  • Each project's GitHub repository, linked above, reviewed November 1, 2026
  • neon1's own repositories for the tools marked in use: https://github.com/neon1llc
  • Stars and activity were used only to find candidates, never as evidence of quality
